subject: Re: Action schedule and commercial milestones for private deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tremblay <sophie.t@edgedata.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed action schedule and evaluation checkpoints for EdgeData private deployment

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I’m attaching a short draft action schedule that maps evaluation checkpoints to commercial milestones for a private/VPC deployment. The goal is to align the technical acceptance test (TAT) and perf checkpoints to a staged commit so you can ramp capacity without upfront over-commit.

High level proposal in the attached EDG-MAP-draft.pdf:
- Week 0–2: Sandbox eval (no platform fee) — 3 test apps, perf targets
- Week 3–6: Pilot (1:1 dev -> prod) — 30% platform fee credit if commit > 6 months
- Post-pilot: staged ramp to reserved capacity with graduated discounts at 3/6/12 months

Attachments: EDG-MAP-draft.pdf, pricing-ramp.xlsx (pricing bands).

Can your team confirm the acceptance tests (latency P95 <= 220ms for 128 tokens, and function-calling reliability >= 99%) are acceptable? If so we’ll convert this into a mutual action schedule and loop in legal for a limited-term SOW.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

--

From: Sophie Tremblay <sophie.t@edgedata.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@edgedata.com>, procurement@edgedata.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposed action schedule and evaluation checkpoints for EdgeData private deployment

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear structure. A few notes from our side after a quick read:
- Acceptance tests: the latency goal looks reasonable but we’ll need a short list of representative queries (we can provide).
- Platform fee: Procurement wants a clearer economics table showing net effective price if we hit each milestone (pilot -> commit -> 6/12 mo). They prefer a platform fee capped at X% after ramp.
- Legal will need a version of the SOW with data residency language and KMS requirements called out.

Question on our side: is Redwood willing to structure the discount as a retroactive credit if we meet the MAP milestones instead of an upfront reduction? That helps our internal budget approvals.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short follow-up with Ravi and procurement next week.

—
Sophie Tremblay
Head of Product | EdgeData Labs
Sophie.T@edgedata.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tremblay <sophie.t@edgedata.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed action schedule and evaluation checkpoints for EdgeData private deployment

Thanks Sophie — that all makes sense. Quick internal notes and answers below, copied here so we’re aligned before legal/procurement jump in: 

- Representative queries: yes please send the list (we’ll run perf across the sample and include a 95th percentile distribution in the pilot report).
- Platform fee credits: We can do a retroactive credit model tied to MAP milestones. Typical structure we’ve used: a refundable credit applied after a successful pilot (up to 30% of platform fee for months 1–3) and staircase discounts applied to reserved capacity once the committed throughput is in place.
- Data residency/KMS: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and can be scoped into the SOW. We’ll add the KMS/HSM requirement to the SOW-outline.docx and send an updated draft for sign-off.

Marcus — can you draft a short commercial summary table (net effective price per token / platform fee % per milestone) we can share with procurement? Neha — loop in Legal to review the SOW additions for KMS/data handling. Laura — heads up that procurement may request an up-front trial exemption on platform fee for the sandbox stage.

Jordan

Subject: Commercial summary / effective pricing by milestone (draft)

Hi all —

Attached is a short commercial summary (pricing-ramp.xlsx) that ties platform-fee credits and reserved capacity discounts to the MAP checkpoints Sophie outlined. Key points:
- Sandbox (Wk0–2): platform fee waived for up to 3 dev seats (no charge).
- Pilot (Wk3–6): platform fee billed at list, with retroactive credit of up to 30% applied to months 1–3 if pilot acceptance tests pass and commit executed within 30 days.
- Committed ramp: 3-tier reserved commitment (Small/Med/Large) with 8%/12%/18% reserved discounts plus a platform fee cap of 5% after month-6 ramp if commit >= 12 months.

I flagged the rows where legal needs to confirm refundability of credits and the timing for retroactive application. Sophie — if procurement is okay with retroactive credits, this should help with approvals.

Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Action schedule and commercial milestones for private deployment

Jordan / Marcus —

Thanks for the detailed draft. Procurement has three clarifying asks before we can move to an internal approval: 
1) Please confirm the mechanism and timing for retroactive credits (credit applied to invoice following successful pilot acceptance and evidence provided). We need the exact appraisal steps documented.
2) We require a cap on total platform fees during the first 12 months (procurement preference: max 5% after ramp).
3) SOW: call out KMS integration points, key rotation responsibilities, and a short list of audit logs that Redwood will provide for the initial 6-month period.

If you can provide an updated SOW-outline.docx and a one-page credit flow (how credits are issued and reconciled) by Monday EOD our procurement team can move to approval conditioned on those terms.

Best,
Procurement Team
EdgeData Labs
procurement@edgedata.com
